transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lara Diaz (Head of ML, Solstice), Tom Brooks (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (PM)

Summary (auto): Intro discovery to map integration patterns. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for conversational search and multi-turn assistants. Main concerns: SDK support (Python/JS), LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy integration, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost), and security (SSO/KMS/audit logs).

Topics: integration SDKs, orchestration (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy and internal API, rate limiting and quotas, observability - traces & cost, pilot & benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Samir my SE is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lara Diaz: Doing well, thanks. We're excited to talk through how Redwood would fit into our stack for the conversational search pilot.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Great, quick agenda - we want to understand your integration surface, typical request volumes, any hard constraints (like VPC or FIPS), and then walk through SDKs and compatibility with LangChain and LlamaIndex. Then outline next steps for a pilot. Sound okay?
[00:25] Priya Nair: Yep that's perfect. I'll just say upfront our product team wants something that can go from prototype to production without rework; so the SDK experience and observability matter a lot.
[00:35] Tom Brooks: From infra, we care about network egress, data residency, and whether we can put a gateway/proxy in front for auth and rate limiting.
[00:42] Maya Chen: Totally. Maybe start with current architecture — Lara, can you give a quick overview of how requests flow today?
[00:49] Lara Diaz: Sure. We have a frontend app that hits our API gateway in GCP. That then fan-outs to a microservice that calls different LLM providers for re-rank and answer generation. Right now most devs use OpenAI via our internal proxy so we can do single sign-on and auditing. We want Redwood to slot into that same pattern, ideally with minimal code change.
[01:12] Samir Patel: Makes sense. Two quick things — SDKs: we have Python and JS SDKs, plus a simple HTTP REST endpoint. For orchestration, we publish small connector examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex, and also a repo showing a lightweight gateway proxy that adds auth and enforces quotas.
[01:30] Tom Brooks: The proxy example — is that a maintained component or just sample code? We prefer a pattern we can run ourselves, not a hosted gateway.
[01:36] Samir Patel: It's sample code intended to be deployed in customer infra — a thin wrapper that adds your auth headers, does JWT validation, and handles local rate limiting before hitting Redwood. Many customers run it behind their API gateway. We also support mutual TLS and VPC peering for Dedicated/Private to avoid public egress.
[01:52] Lara Diaz: Okay. On orchestration side, our ML engineers use LangChain in Python and rely on LlamaIndex for indexing product catalog embeddings. We need to know if Redwood plays nicely with that stack — are there ready-made chains or index connectors?
[02:07] Samir Patel: Yes, we have examples: a LangChain LLM wrapper that implements the standard call signature, and an embeddings client that behaves like the common embedding API so it should plug into LlamaIndex with minimal glue. We also publish a notebook showing batching and caching patterns for lower token cost.
[02:22] Priya Nair: How about streaming compatibility? Our chat UI needs token-by-token streaming for lower latency perceived by users.
[02:29] Maya Chen: We support streaming responses in our Hosted API and Streaming is also available over websocket for Dedicated. There are some small differences in how the SDK surfaces cancelation and callbacks, but we have examples for both React and Node streaming clients.
[02:44] Tom Brooks: Rate-limits — how are those enforced? We need per-customer and per-route quotas. Right now we enforce at gateway level but we'd like Redwood to enforce burst protection too.
[02:54] Samir Patel: On Hosted, we expose per-API-key rate limits and adjustable quotas per account. For Dedicated you can configure instance-level token throughput and set token per-minute quotas. We also provide headers on each response showing remaining tokens/quota and a dedicated dashboard that allows you to set per-route caps. If you deploy a proxy you can keep the gateway layer and have Redwood as a backstop.
[03:17] Lara Diaz: Good. Observability — what hooks do we get for tracing, token-level cost, and per-request metadata?
[03:24] Samir Patel: We emit request-level metadata (model, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency) and integrate with OpenTelemetry for traces. We also have a Redwood Console where you can see token cost per route and export to your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private we can push logs to your S3/GCS or to a customer-managed ELK/Kafka.
[03:42] Tom Brooks: Do you support passing our trace id and get that correlated in Redwood traces?
[03:46] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pass X-Trace-Id or an OpenTelemetry header and it surfaces in the Console logs. We try to preserve incoming trace context.
[03:55] Priya Nair: Security questions: SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS for key management — do you have documentation?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share our security pack. Hosted is SOC 2 Type II and we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For Dedicated or Private we can integrate with your KMS or HSM for model/key encryption. We'll attach the security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[04:16] Lara Diaz: On model variants — we want to evaluate a smaller quantized model for embeddings and a larger one for generation. Can we pin models and have fallback to cheaper variants if latency spikes?
[04:27] Samir Patel: Absolutely. Our routing policies let you pin model versions per-route, and we support automatic fallbacks to compatible quantized variants if the primary is unavailable. For Dedicated you can deploy multiple model variants to the same pool and set weightings or canary rules.
[04:41] Tom Brooks: For the pilot, our traffic pattern is bursty — 300 QPS at peak for re-rank calls, average prompt size ~600 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. For chat assistant less calls but longer context window. Will your batching help reduce cost without harming latency?
[04:58] Samir Patel: Yes, our serving runtime does continuous batching and KV cache reuse for multi-turn to reduce cost. For that QPS profile we'd probably recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale and prefix caching — but we can run a bench to confirm.
[05:12] Priya Nair: About LangChain — are there async examples? Our stack uses async Python and we want to avoid thread blocking.
[05:19] Samir Patel: We have async clients in Python and Node. The LangChain connector supports async LLM calls; we'll share the repo. There are small differences in generative streaming handling between sync and async, but it's documented.
[05:31] Lara Diaz: What about LlamaIndex — any gotchas around embedding size or rate limits when indexing large catalogs?
[05:38] Samir Patel: For large indexing jobs we recommend batching embeddings and using our bulk embeddings endpoint; that can be run from a worker pool and we have guidance for backoff and retry semantics. Quotas can be increased for batch jobs during indexing windows.
[05:51] Tom Brooks: Network: Can we do VPC peering so calls never traverse the public internet?
[05:55] Maya Chen: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and private endpoints. For Hosted customers we also offer customer-managed proxy patterns so traffic still goes through your infra first.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Licensing and cost — we want an estimate for monthly costs for a 3-month pilot: 300 QPS re-rank plus chat assistant with a few thousand users.
[06:15] Maya Chen: I'll send a pricing matrix that shows per-token hosted rates and a sample Dedicated commit profile. For the pilot we often start with Hosted for speed, then shift to Dedicated when you have predictable throughput — we'll model both.
[06:25] Lara Diaz: One last technical detail — do you provide SDK hooks for token attribution so our product analytics can break down cost per feature?
[06:32] Samir Patel: We provide token-level breakdowns and metadata tagging on each request so you can add feature tags. The Console will also let you filter by route or tag to see cost per feature.
[06:44] Tom Brooks: Potential blockers: we need the security pack, examples of the gateway proxy, and proof that OpenTelemetry headers are preserved end-to-end.
[06:53] Maya Chen: We'll include the security pack and a short demo repo for the proxy. Samir will include an OpenTelemetry trace example.
[07:00] Priya Nair: Great. Can we schedule a technical deep dive next week to do a bench run?
[07:05] Maya Chen: Yes, Samir and I are available week of 5/18. We'll propose times after the call.
[07:10] Lara Diaz: If we go Dedicated, what is the onboarding timeline?
[07:13] Maya Chen: Typically provision within 2-4 weeks for Dedicated depending on capacity and region, and Private (VPC) can be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals. For pilots most customers start with Hosted and then transition.
[07:25] Tom Brooks: One more thing — retention and audit logs. We need at least 90-day audit logs and the ability to set retention policy.
[07:32] Samir Patel: Yes, retention policies are configurable for logs; for Hosted we have default retention but can extend as an add-on. For Dedicated you manage storage; we can ship logs to your bucket with any retention you need.
[07:45] Priya Nair: Ok I think that's all from our side.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Awesome — recap of next steps: Maya will send pricing and security pack; Samir will share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, proxy repo, and OpenTelemetry sample; Tom to send request patterns and QPS numbers; Priya to confirm stakeholders and pilot dates.
[07:59] Lara Diaz: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[08:01] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up by end of day with the docs and a proposed time for the deep dive.

(Transcript note: occasional mis-transcriptions: "Redwood" appears sometimes as "Redwooded" in auto- text, some proper nouns like LlamaIndex transcribed as "Lama Index" and OpenTelemetry sometimes as "open telem" )

References shared in call: link: /redwood/docs/langchain-connector, link: /redwood/examples/proxy-gateway, link: /redwood/security/security-pack.pdf

End of transcript.
